findings.evidence: the GPU was saturated, so the test's load was enough (not measured: prompt-work share); prefill against its ceiling stood in for the prompt-work share
requests spent 1% of their time to first token queued; the engine chose the concurrency cap, so it cannot say whether the cap held them
TTFT p50 1538 ms is 13x TPOT p50 122.5 ms
steps carried 220 tokens on average against a budget of 2048, with 0 requests waiting
TPOT p95 142.2 ms is 1.2x p50 122.5 ms
decode ran at 49% of the memory-bandwidth ceiling at the measured batch

the GPU was saturated at its power limit (busy 100%, at 72 of 72 W, SM clock 1158 of 2040 MHz): server settings that run more at once cannot add throughput here; what can is less work per request (shorter prompts or answers, cached shared prompts), a smaller or quantized model, or a faster GPU
the API server used 0.05 CPU cores over the window
a decode step reads 0.34x as many KV-cache bytes as weight bytes (average context 5333 tokens, batch 15.8)
speculation is off or not reported

diagnosis.shape: 13.0 prompt tokens computed per generated token

decode_of_ceiling.meaning: decode tokens/s as a percent of the memory-bandwidth ceiling
decode_of_ceiling.name: decode_of_ceiling
decode_of_ceiling.source: set from Tensward's runs on L4 and A10G that induced and avoided this bottleneck (Databricks measured 55-60% bandwidth use at batch 1)

frontend_cpu.meaning: CPU cores the engine's API-server process used over the window
frontend_cpu.name: frontend_cpu
frontend_cpu.source: no published cut-off; the API server is one process, so about one core is its ceiling; not yet calibrated

gpu_idle.meaning: share of the traced window the GPU sat idle, in gaps of at least 50 us
gpu_idle.name: gpu_idle
gpu_idle.source: no published cut-off; Tensward's runs showed 70-81% idle with CUDA graphs off on a 0.5B model; not yet checked on runs without host overhead

kv_over_weights.meaning: KV-cache bytes a decode step reads over the weight bytes
kv_over_weights.name: kv_over_weights
kv_over_weights.source: no published cut-off; MagicDec shows KV reads limit decode at large batch and long context

kv_peak.meaning: highest sampled share of the engine's KV-cache pool in use
kv_peak.name: kv_peak
kv_peak.source: documented serving guidance on KV usage

preemption_rate.name: preemption_rate
preemption_rate.source: vLLM docs give no rate; Llumnix (OSDI'24) saw 8% of requests preempted

prompt_work.meaning: share of the engine's busy time spent on prompt work
prompt_work.name: prompt_work
prompt_work.source: the share of the engine's measured prompt capacity at which prompt work names the bottleneck; the critical level is where the A10G's prompt-bound runs sat

queue_share.meaning: share of server-side TTFT spent queued before scheduling
queue_share.name: queue_share
queue_share.source: set from Tensward's runs on L4 and A10G that induced and avoided this bottleneck (no published cut-off)

spec_acceptance.meaning: tokens per speculative draft (1 + accepted tokens per draft)
spec_acceptance.name: spec_acceptance
spec_acceptance.source: no published cut-off; speculation pays only when acceptance beats the draft's cost

spec_coverage.meaning: share of generated tokens that came from accepted drafts
spec_coverage.name: spec_coverage
spec_coverage.source: no published cut-off; Tensward's runs lost throughput at about 5% coverage with 32 clients and gained at about 43% with 1 client; low coverage at low concurrency not yet measured

tensor_busy.meaning: tensor-pipe busy percent of the kernel with the most GPU time
tensor_busy.name: tensor_busy
tensor_busy.source: no published cut-off; measured from kernel counters, never inferred from batch size

tpot_tail.name: tpot_tail
tpot_tail.source: Sarathi-Serve (OSDI'24) shows the stalls; no published ratio

ttft_over_tpot.name: ttft_over_tpot
ttft_over_tpot.source: no published cut-off; a starting point until calibrated on GPUs
